catalogue_requests.reason: the catalogue has no class that switches a thermal actuator off without a target temperature (cap.motion.stop.v1 is for motion); this package uses an x-cap id with an inline output schema as its safe-state action
catalogue_requests.summary: Switch the TEC controller off (command 0x71 state 0x00) and leave the cooling fan on (command 0x70 state 0x01); this is the safe state.

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names helper PythonObjectDriver, but OceanOpticsTEC sends framed binary USB commands (a command byte plus little-endian fields, oceanoptics/base.py:317-395), so a command table or a plain object wrapper cannot express the interface; this package is a direct Driver over the upstream class with a native.py factory. NOT COVERED: the spectrometer spectrum array (wavelengths and intensities) and the integration-time/acquisition methods of the upstream OceanOpticsBase; the card's entry symbol is OceanOpticsTEC, the TEC controller only, and this driver exposes that class's thermal scalar functions. The TEC setpoint range is operator_required because no text of the clone states one (the -17 in initialize_TEC is a chosen method default, oceanoptics/base.py:398-404); site-limits.example.json is an example overlay for this bench, not a statement about any unit. The fake is an in-memory stand-in with placeholder start values marked in fake.py, not a recording of the device; the hardware path in native.py was never run. This package is model-authored and unreviewed, so the loader refuses the R2 hardware backend until a human sets reviewed_by in driver.lock.json. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not a package file.
